key_insight: Hybrid Memory splits memory into complementary roles—precise long-term archival for static backgrounds and vigilant short-term tracking for dynamic subjects—so objects that go out of sight are preserved and correctly re-integrated when they reappear.
problem_solved: Existing video world models treat environments as largely static and fail when dynamic subjects become occluded: objects can freeze, distort, or disappear after temporary occlusion or leaving the frame.
method: Dual-memory architecture: a long-term archival store for static scene content + a short-term, identity-aware tracker for dynamic subjects.
Occlusion- and reappearance-aware read/write rules that maintain persistent object identities and motion cues while updating background geometry.
Integrate hybrid memory into video world-model training to improve simulation, prediction, and re-rendering across occlusions and temporal gaps.
impact: Provides more robust, realistic video world models that preserve object continuity across occlusions—beneficial for simulation, planning, robotics, and downstream prediction tasks where object persistence matters.

paper_title: Out of Sight but Not Out of Mind: Hybrid Memory for Dynamic Video World Models
paper_authors: Kaijin Chen, Dingkang Liang, Xin Zhou, Yikang Ding, Xiaoqiang Liu
